basics.name: David Bannister
basics.label: Data Analytics Engineer
basics.summary: Data professional specializing in SQL, Python, and workflow automation, building reliable data pipelines and reporting solutions that support business decisions.

work.name: University of Hawaii Foundation
highlights: Delivered 40+ custom SQL data solutions each month for executive leadership and department stakeholders, enabling targeted outreach and strategic decision-making.
Designed executive reporting solutions using Oracle PL/SQL and Crystal Reports to monitor organizational performance and business metrics.
Developed and maintained Oracle PL/SQL packages supporting overnight ETL workflows, external integrations, scheduled imports/exports, and production data pipelines.
Designed and implemented an automated Alteryx workflow integrating internal Oracle databases with the Mailchimp API for marketing campaign analytics.
Automated recurring data ingestion and reporting workflows with Alteryx, reducing manual processing by approximately 16 hours per week and removing the need for an additional student worker position.

work.name: Honolulu Disposal Service
highlights: Built an ETL pipeline to cleanse, transform, and load over five years of operational data into Microsoft SQL Server for enterprise reporting.
Developed interactive Power BI and Streamlit dashboards that identified statistically significant underperforming assets through operational analytics.
Performed statistical analysis and hypothesis testing on assets exceeding $200K in operating costs, supporting executive investment decisions.

work.name: ITS Help Desk
highlights: Resolved client technical issues using Microsoft and Google suite products, created reports, and monitored UH user systems. Provided technical solutions and expertise.

courses: Focus on Econometrics, Statistics, and Research Methods; Dean’s List distinction.
Studied abroad in Florence, Italy, at Lorenzo de Medici during Fall 2022 and Fall 2023.

publications.name: Kurtosis: a Poor Measure of Tail Risk (Research in Progress)
publications.summary: Research in progress. Developed 20+ statistical models of probability distributions using Python without direct probability functions and Streamlit, displaying relationships among kurtosis, mean, variance, and standard deviation as parameters changed.
